land.text: the Yamato realm: 'the Emperor of Japan ruled relatively uncontested from modern-day Nara Prefecture, then known as Yamato Province' and the court 'exercised power over clans in Kyushu and Honshu'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria lacks Yamato before 540; the jk-01-x additions batch writes it (slug to confirm; 'yamato' assumed).

land.text: the whole realm: 'Japan's capital is moved from Fujiwara-kyō to Heijō-kyō' in 710

capitals.name: Asuka (Asuka, Nara Prefecture)
capitals.note: 'an imperial court attended by subordinate clan chieftains but with no permanent capital', moving among palaces in the Asuka region; the Naniwa (645-654) and Ōmi (667-672) courts are not on the page.

capitals.name: Fujiwara-kyō (Kashihara)
capitals.note: '694: The imperial capital is moved to Fujiwara-kyō, in present-day Kashihara city.'

correction.text: the realm as Cliopatria draws it from 540, two years earlier: the period is 'lasting from 538 to 710'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the row in 540; the page dates the period from 538 (the traditional arrival of Buddhism), 'although its beginning could be said to overlap with the preceding Kofun period'.

230,061 km2 for 540-704: Honshu to about 38 N, Shikoku and Kyushu; no page opened gives an area. The northern limit is generous for the 6th century (the first forts on the Sendai plain date from 724 and 'the fort of Ideha' near Akita from 709, Emishi page) and Tsushima (129.2-129.5 E) lies outside the bbox although it was a province; both unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged; holds 705 to 710, when the capital moves to Heijō-kyō

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria ends the row in 709; the page ends the period in 710. The 705 break is unexplained (identical area).

region.text: the Yamato realm ruled 'from modern-day Nara Prefecture, then known as Yamato Province'

ledger.note: 538: the Asuka period opens; the Yamato court rules from Yamato Province. 'lasting from 538 to 710'; 'the Emperor of Japan ruled relatively uncontested from modern-day Nara Prefecture, then known as Yamato Province'; before the Taika Reform the court 'exercised power over clans in Kyushu and Honshu'. The year is a cultural date, not a border event; Cliopatria starts the row in 540.
694: the capital moves to Fujiwara-kyō. '694: The imperial capital is moved to Fujiwara-kyō, in present-day Kashihara city.'

region.text: 'the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita'

ledger.note: 709: the Ideha (Dewa) stockade on the Japan Sea coast. 'In 709 the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita'; the territory between Akita and the northwest was 'not under government control'. Cliopatria's shape stops at 38.2 N; the gain is a coastal foothold the rendering agent adds.

region.text: the whole realm passes to the court at Heijō-kyō

ledger.note: 710: the capital moves to Heijō-kyō (Nara); the Asuka period ends. 'lasting from 538 to 710'; the Nara page: 'Japan's capital is moved from Fujiwara-kyō to Heijō-kyō'.

wars.name: Abe no Hirafu's northern expeditions
wars.outcome: 'An alliance with Aguta Emishi, Tsugaru Emishi and Watarishima Emishi was formed by Abe' (658); no land was held.
wars.note: 'The expedition happens to be the furthest northern penetration of the Japanese Imperial army until the 16th century' (Aguta is present-day Akita Prefecture, Watarishima Hokkaidō). The page dates only 658; the later voyages are not on it.

wars.name: Battle of Baekgang
wars.outcome: '663: The Japanese navy was defeated by the Silla-Tang alliance in Battle of Baekgang, failing to restore Baekje.'
wars.note: 'Yamato deployed its navy to aid Baekje, in 660–663, against an invasion by Silla and Tang China.' Fought in Korea; no Japanese land involved.

wars.name: Jinshin War
wars.outcome: '672: Prince Ōama, later Emperor Tenmu usurped the throne by winning the Jinshin no Ran civil war.'
wars.note: A succession war of months inside the realm; no border moved.

certainty.note: No treaty line anywhere: the northern frontier against the Emishi is a zone of stockades (Ideha 709); the Hayato of southern Kyushu and the islands (Tsushima, Iki, the Ryukyus) are not on the pages opened.

sources.title: Asuka period
sources.note: Identity, 538-710, Fujiwara-kyō 694, Baekgang 663, Jinshin 672, the extent 'clans in Kyushu and Honshu'; no area figure.

sources.title: Emishi
sources.note: The northern frontier: Abe no Hirafu 658, Ideha 709, Taga 724.

notes: Cliopatria 540-709 against the page's 538-710: a new keyframe 538-539 and a one-year overlap with Nara Japan in 710 (the successor's found event takes the land). Predecessor: Yamato before 540, which Cliopatria lacks and the jk-01-x additions batch writes; the slug 'yamato' is assumed and must be reconciled. Counterpart 'emishi' is used for the frontier gains of all three Japanese court dossiers (Asuka, Nara, Heian); no row covers the Emishi, so either a dossier of that slug is written or the gains are read as from nobody. Tsushima lies outside the bbox of every Asuka, Nara and Heian shape; the Heian dossier adds it from the Toi invasion page ('Tsushima and Iki provinces'); for the Asuka shapes it is noted, not corrected (page budget). Not on the pages opened: the Taika Reform's provincial system beyond 'The country was divided into provinces headed by governors appointed by the court' (645-646), the Hayato, the Naniwa and Ōmi courts, Abe no Hirafu's 659-660 voyages, the Taihō Code's provinces (701).
